newsitem.title: GREECE: TVX GOLD THREATENS TO HALT GREEK OPERATION OCT 23.
newsitem.headline: TVX GOLD THREATENS TO HALT GREEK OPERATION OCT 23.

text.p: The Greek subsidiary of Canada's TVX Gold said it will suspend its northern Greek gold mining project on October 23 unless local residents stop blocking the main access road to the mines.
TVX Gold paid $270 million for the Kassandra mines last December but operations have been stymied from the outset by residents who say it will damage the local environment and tourist industry.
TVX Gold Hellas, the Greek subsidiary, said in its statement that suspending work was in effect a declaration of force majeure, which means that it will stop paying salaries to all 600 workers.

"TVX Hellas, owner of the Cassandra mines, after a 10-month illegal disruption of work and operations at the main Olympiada mine, announces that because of this protracted situation it is forced to suspend mining and other operations starting October 23," the TVX Hellas statement said.

TVX Gold said recently it had invested $28 million so far in developing the Cassandra mines. The company is relying on the mines to keep its promise to shareholders to produce 1.1 million ounces of gold a year by the year 2000, versus 423,000 ounces in 1995.

TVX Gold's purchase of the mines near the northern port of Salonika and its plan to build a gold-processing plant was the biggest foreign investment in Greece in 30 years. --Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
